npcs.name: Doug, relief guard at the end of the wire

nodes.line: Randwick City Council, assets. I need someone who isn't scared of heights and won't ask too many questions about the register.
Asset 0041. Coogee Pier. Opened 1928 with a ballroom and a picture theatre. The swell had most of it by 1934 and a contractor carted off the rest. It has been inspected annually ever since.

choices.text: Then why is it still on the register?
Where does the register say it is?

nodes.line: You can't delete an asset. You can only revalue it. To revalue it you need a current photograph of the asset. I have been explaining that sentence since 2011.

choices.text: So photograph the empty air and you can write it off.

nodes.line: Digitised in 1994 off the 1928 survey, wrong datum. Officially the pier now stands in High Cross Park. The kiosk is in Kingsford. They drifted separately. The register is the authority, not the ocean.

choices.text: High Cross Park is nowhere near the water.

nodes.line: Annual inspection, Asset 0041. Photograph it at its registered coordinates, both parts, and log the travel or finance won't pay the claim. It's a day's work and it's a real job number.

nodes.line: It's a structure over water, so you need the working at heights ticket. I know there's no structure. I know the water is in Coogee. Do the course.

improv.persona: Neville, an asset officer at Randwick City Council in Sydney's east, grade five, thirty-one years in local government. Deadpan, unhurried, faintly proud of the register. No exclamation marks.

npcs.name: Coralie, Crows Nest traffic safety working group
